listings.title: The Parker & Neal Mola Collection - Part 2
listings.description: Click Here to BID on this Online Auction!! The Parker & Neal Mola Collection Auction on August 22nd presents a compelling selection of molas drawn from the renowned collection of Ann Parker and Avon Neal, co-authors of Molas: Folk Art of the Cuna Indians. The auction features a diverse range of molas showcasing the rich artistic traditions of the Kuna (Guna) people of Panama. Collectors will find intricate reverse appliqué work with multiple fabric layers, finely executed geometric designs, and expressive figural compositions. Many pieces reflect mid-20th century production, a period prized for its balance of technical skill and bold design, while others illustrate later stylistic developments with vibrant color and graphic impact. Motifs range from traditional patterns to depictions of animals, birds, religious, and narrative scenes, demonstrating both cultural symbolism and individual artistic creativity. The selection emphasizes strong design, quality craftsmanship, and visual appeal, making it ideal for both seasoned collectors and those new to molas. This second and last offering also includes many Guna Nuchu Carved Wood Medicine Figures. This auction offers a rare opportunity to acquire works from a historically significant and well-documented collection. Click Here to BID on this Online Auction!!

listings.title: Books & Manuscripts, Including Americana
listings.description: Freeman’s August 20, 2026, Books & Manuscripts, Including Americana sale highlights the continued celebration of the 250th anniversary of the founding of America. It includes important documents related to the American Revolution, Presidential history, the African-American experience, fine works of literature, natural history, and much more. The sale is led by an extremely rare 1781 French loan document printed and signed by Benjamin Franklin and used to help fund the American Revolution (est. $200,000-$300,000); a first edition of The Book of Mormon ($100,000-$150,000); and two very important letters signed by President George Washington, one transmitting the first major law passed by Congress ($100,000-$150,000), and the other reaffirming the American Treaty of Friendship with Morocco ($50,000-$80,000). Other highlights include the Surveying Commission of the Continental Congress settling the New York/Massachusetts border ($30,000-$50,000); a very rare book signed by famed astrophysicist Stephen Hawking ($15,000-$25,000); a rare letter signed by early African-American businessman Paul Cuffe ($15,000-$25,000); autograph notes in the hand of Dr. Charles A. Leale, the first physician on site after the assassination of Abraham Lincoln ($12,000-$18,000); a large collection of printed and manuscript documents fresh to market from Rev. Samuel J. May, a founding member of the New England Anti-Slavery Society in the 1830s, and a lifetime ardent supporter of the abolitionist movement.
